title: Does bundle adjustment repair wrong camera poses in a multi-view reconstruction?
lede: with 12 views, 0.5 px noise and every camera pose wrong, bundle adjustment cuts mean surface error from 0.0117 to 0.0014 object radii (the true-pose floor), 8× here and 73× at 0.2 radii of position error, but only 1.4× at 4 px of pixel noise and not at all with 4 views. Synthetic only
summary: Follows sensing-recon, which found a 1° camera pose error costs as much as about 2 px of pixel noise. On the same synthetic bumpy-ellipsoid rig, every camera gets a random rotation (0–4° per axis) and position (0–0.2 object radii) error; sparse bundle adjustment (SciPy least_squares) then refines all poses and points from the wrong-pose triangulation, and both are scored after a similarity alignment. With 12 views, 0.5 px noise, 0.5° and 0.02 radii the mean surface error falls from 0.0117 to 0.0014, equal to triangulation with true poses; the gain is 73× at 0.2 radii of position error but only 1.4× at 4 px noise (where pixel noise sets the error) and 0.9× with 4 views. A pose prior with the true sigma changed nothing. Limits: synthetic, matches given and correct, no outliers, known intrinsics, a start close to the truth, and alignment to the true points; 8 seeds per cell.
